issues.description: Method name mismatch for Bitmap24 file-writing API: the template repository header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) declares a method named write(const std::string &i_filename), while the template repository implementation (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) defines Bitmap24::save(const std::string &i_filename) and the example usage in main.cpp (example_program/src/main.cpp) calls bitmap.save(...). The solution repository consistently uses save(...). This naming inconsistency in the template header vs implementation/usage will cause compilation errors (missing symbol or unresolved reference) and confuses students about which API to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template header with implementation and usage by changing the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from write(const std::string &i_filename) to save(const std::string &i_filename); (preferred, matches the solution). Alternatively, rename the implementation and all call sites to write(...). Update any accompanying documentation to reflect the chosen API name so students can compile and run the example program without linker or missing-declaration errors.

issues.description: The Bitmap file output method is named inconsistently across template artifacts: the class declaration in template/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp declares a method named write(const std::string &i_filename) (line 47), but the implementation in template/example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp defines Bitmap24::save(const std::string &i_filename) (lines 78-160). Example usage in template/example_program/src/main.cpp calls bitmap.save(outfile) (line 228), so the header-declared name (write) does not match either the implementation or usage (save). The solution repository consistently uses save(const std::string&) in both the header and implementation. This mismatch prevents a clear mapping for students (which identifier to implement or call) and will cause compilation errors or blocking confusion when building the example program.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the declaration in the template header with the implementation and usage. Change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from write(const std::string &i_filename) to save(const std::string &i_filename) so it matches Bitmap24::save(...) in Bitmap24.cpp and the usage in main.cpp. This matches the solution repository and prevents compile-time errors and student confusion.
